data.name: The Agency of Anomalies: Mystic Hospital Collector's Edition
data.detailed_description:
Become a special agent and investigate a military hospital that hosted a variety of terrifying experiments in The Agency of Anomalies: Mystic Hospital! Discover the monstrosities that soldiers, doctors, and nurses have been transformed into, as you explore every single room of the hospital. Dive into this dark Hidden Object Puzzle Adventure game and stop a dimensional vortex from destroying the world!

- Fantastic locations
- Terrifying creatures
- Explore haunted military hospitals!

reviews.review:
Having played The Agency of Anomalies: Mystic Hospital years ago, it had always been one of my favorite HOGs.  When it mysteriously appeared in the New Releases here on Steam, I knew without a doubt I needed to play it again.  However, as I booted up this classic, I questioned just what was it about the game that left such a mark on my memory; the artwork is good, but it’s nothing that stands out among others in the genre (or even the series itself), and the gameplay is your typical HOPA-fare.  But as I stepped into the agency investigator’s shoes yet again, this time with a few years of HOG-playing experience under my belt, I was better equipped to pick out all the things that make this title one of the best the genre has to offer. 

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=734344930
Set in the post WWI era, the Agency of Anomalies has been contacted by one Dr. Oliver Orvos, a German doctor, scientist, and the sole survivor of a horrific incident that occurred 10 years prior at a top secret military hospital.  Recent events lead him to believe that a dimensional vortex may surface at the abandoned installation, and he’s in desperate need of someone to investigate and deter this paranormal phenomenon before it risks tearing apart the very fabric of existence itself!  As the Agency’s top investigator, you must uncover the hospital’s secrets in order to prevent a world-ending cataclysm.  Nope, this isn’t your typical HOG story, but that’s one of the things I enjoy so much about it.  One can only take so many haunted houses and magical fantasy worlds before boredom sets in.   Traversing this abandoned military facility is a welcome divergence from the stereotypically colorful settings that fill the genre these days. 

Gameplay itself is pretty standard “adventure lite” fare, but it’s the little details that make it stand out.  The addition of secret animations that play on certain clicked items breathe life and atmosphere into the empty world, even if they’re only tricks of the Agent’s mind.   I also appreciate the era appropriate items in the hidden object scenes which help immerse the player in the time period.  The scenes themselves are well composed with plenty of objects to search through, but nothing so obscured as to feel unfairly hidden, that is as long as one has enough patience to look carefully.  The item that is to be added to your inventory is the final one to appear on your list after all others are found, which makes it feel as if there’s a purpose to searching through all that junk.  Although it’s such a little thing, it adds a lot. 

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=733423166
But above all else, it’s the writing that distinguishes Mystic Hospital from the rest.  The main character is written so well, his personality oozes from the commentary and journal entries.  You can tell this is a guy who’s seen it all, nothing phases him, and he’s gonna finish the job no matter what it takes.  He’s witty and sarcastic and dangit, I wish he had a name, but I’ll just have to settle for Agent.  

Then there’s the patient files which are narrated by the good doctor, giving us an interesting glimpse into the experiments performed on the hospital patients which ultimately lead to catastrophe.  The voice actor does a wonderful job of describing the events that took place without hamming it up with the usual HOG camp.  The inclusion of beautifully painted, sepia-colored art pieces serve as a pleasing complement, and contrast, to the grittiness of the rest of the game's graphics.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=739306365
As much as I loved the main adventure, it pains me to note how disappointing the bonus chapter was.   Usually these extra snippets give additional background into the plot and characters, but it merely included a few documents hinting at the sequel, and not much beyond that.  This would have been fine should the gameplay have been engaging enough, but the additional play time was padded with so many hidden object scenes that even I had grown weary of them towards the end.  I still recommend playing through it, because why not?  But I really wish we would’ve been given more information on the hospital, the villain, or even the protagonist himself.  

Small grievances aside, Mystic Hospital remains one of the best HOGs I’ve played.  Perhaps the artwork and premise may not appeal to those used to more brightly painted titles, but the gameplay, atmosphere and writing is truly some of the best I’ve come across in the genre.  I certainly hope the rest of the series makes it over, as I cannot wait to experience more of this Agent’s paranormal adventures.   

Bottom Line: Highly Recommended.
